description: As a Marvel fan, especially of Iron Man, I built a motorized helmet inspired by the Mark V armor in 2025. This personal project brings together 3D printing, electronics and embedded programming.

I completed the build on my own: 3D printing the parts, mechanical assembly, electronic integration, wiring and ESP32 programming. Servomotors move the individual sections of the faceplate, requiring coordinated control matched to the mechanism.
The photographs show the assembled helmet and its interior, including the wiring, servomotors and linkages. Integrating these components into a compact space was an essential part of the build.
This project let me put a complete mechatronics workflow into practice, from manufacturing parts to embedded control. All I need now is J.A.R.V.I.S. and an arc reactor… the helmet is a good start.
The STL button links to BoxAndLoop’s Mark V helmet on Thingiverse, a downloadable model of this helmet type. My ESP32 code will be shared later.
